Gemini CLI edit hook

Gemini CLI's AfterTool hook runs after a tool executes. Offing registers it for the write_file and replace tools, reads tool_input.file_path, takes the project root from cwd (with GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR as the documented fallback), and answers in the JSON documented for Gemini CLI 0.67.0 (current stable, 2026-11-04) at https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/hooks/reference.md: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext is appended to the tool result in the model's context, systemMessage is shown in the terminal, and the hook exits 0 — the tool has already run, so this is feedback the model acts on in the same turn, never an error. No findings, or any hook failure, prints nothing and exits 0.

npx @velella/offing init --hooks-for gemini --dry-run   # show the diff first
npx @velella/offing init --hooks-for gemini             # merge into .gemini/settings.json

The command writes only the project-level file Gemini CLI documents, <repo>/.gemini/settings.json — never anything in your home directory — keeps every existing setting and hook (including mcpServers), and appends one AfterTool entry. Running it again changes nothing:

{
  "hooks": {
    "AfterTool": [
      {
        "matcher": "write_file|replace",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "name": "offing",
            "type": "command",
            "command": "npx --no-install offing hook gemini",
            "timeout": 60000
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

matcher is a regular expression for tool events, and timeout is in milliseconds, so 60000 is Gemini CLI's documented default of one minute; Offing's own budget stays ten seconds, so a slow scan fails open instead of holding the turn. To turn it off, delete that AfterTool entry, or remove the whole .gemini/settings.json if Offing wrote it.

The transcript below is real output from the built CLI on 2026-11-07, against the fixture repository in tests/fixtures/agent-hooks/gemini/repo with the AfterTool payload in write-file.json (its cwd pointed at that repository):

$ cat Dockerfile
FROM node:16
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
CMD ["node", "index.js"]

$ node dist/src/cli.js hook gemini < aftertool.json
{
  "systemMessage": "Offing found 1 lifecycle issue in the files just changed.",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "AfterTool",
    "additionalContext": "Offing found 1 lifecycle issue in Dockerfile:\n1) [high] Node.js image release lines 21 and older are end-of-life — Dockerfile:1\n   Replacement: A node image on a supported release line, such as node:22\n   Evidence: https://nodejs.org/en/about/eol\n\nFix this before continuing; nothing was changed automatically."
  }
}
$ echo $?
0

Gemini CLI appends that additionalContext to the tool result, which rewrites the base image in the same turn. The same payload for a file with no findings then exits 0 with no output:

$ sed -i 's/node:16/node:22/' Dockerfile

$ node dist/src/cli.js hook gemini < aftertool.json
$ echo $?
0
